text:
Noah: Hey team, first-day weirdness. My company MBP enrolled but FileVault says "Not enabled" and I keep getting a prompt during login: 'Unable to contact device management server to escrow FileVault key'. I'm at a coffee shop on their Wi-Fi — could that be it? macOS 14.3.1. Blocker for getting Docker installed.

Priti (IT): Welcome Noah! Yep, captive portals frequently block MDM network calls during the initial enrollment/escrow steps. Quick checks: run `fdesetup status` and `sudo profiles status -type enrollment` and paste outputs. Also, are you behind any captive portal (login/accept terms) or a VPN?

Noah: Outputs below, I'm on the coffee place Wi-Fi and didn't sign any portal (my phone has the hotspot but I wanted to avoid tethering).

``` 
$ fdesetup status
FileVault is Off.
No user is enabled for FileVault.

$ sudo profiles status -type enrollment
Enrolled: Yes
Profile identifier: com.redwood.mdm.enroll
Last check-in: 2026-12-06T09:02:10Z
Device compliance: pending (FileVault not enabled)
```

Claire (Buddy): @Noah I hit this last week — I had to join a network that allowed device traffic (corporate or my phone hotspot) so the MDM could reach the escrow endpoint. Coffee shops sometimes intercept calls and return HTML, which breaks the MDM's REST calls.

Priti (IT): Confirmed. Because the device is supervised we can do the institutional escrow flow, but the device must be able to reach MDM endpoints during the push. Two options: 1) Connect to a network without captive portal (home Wi-Fi, tether to phone), accept any captive portal if needed, then reply here and I'll re-push the FileVault enable; 2) If you prefer, bring the device to an office and we'll finish in person. Which do you want?

Noah: I can tether to my phone quickly. Will switch and report back.

Noah: Switched to hotspot and ran the checks again after giving it ~30s for profiles to sync. Paste outputs: 

```
$ sudo profiles status -type enrollment
Enrolled: Yes
Profile identifier: com.redwood.mdm.enroll
Last check-in: 2026-12-06T09:18:42Z
Device compliance: pending (FileVault not enabled)
```

Priti (IT): Great — I'm pushing the "Enable FileVault (institutional escrow)" command now. You should see a modal: "Redwood Device Management requests to enable FileVault using the organization's recovery key." Click Accept and enter your macOS password. Reboot when prompted.

MDM Bot: Pushing FileVault enable (institutional escrow) for device id c4b2a7. Expected user action: Accept prompt, enter password, reboot.

Noah: Got the modal, accepted and entered password. It shows "Enabling FileVault..." and asked to reboot. Rebooting now.

Noah: Post-reboot `fdesetup status` shows: 

```
FileVault is On.
Users enabled for FileVault:
 - noah
```
System Settings now shows FileVault: On. No more escrow error. Docker installed fine after that.

Priti (IT): Closing notes: captive portals or filtered networks can block MDM escrow calls. If you hit this, switch to a non-captive network or tether and ask IT to re-push the escrow command. If the device is unsupervised we have different steps, file a ticket in that case.

Claire (Buddy): Welcome and congrats Noah :tada: — glad it was just a hotspot!

MDM Bot: Ticket IT-1402: FileVault escrow completed via hotspot for device c4b2a7.
